source_selection_rule: Deduplicate by original scholarly experiment, not by edition/URL or cited preprint. Prefer directly accessible original publisher, code and author data. Keep separately evidenced claims distinct.

related_existing_in_progress_pr.scope: Bartling & Srinivasan (2025) B consent demand vs architect conditional supply; avoid reusing as independent new study or overwriting concurrent audit.

sources.title: Distinguishing between intrinsic and instrumental sources of the value of choice
sources.authors: Sean Devine; Kevin da Silva Castanheira; Stephen M. Fleming; A. Ross Otto
sources.reported_effect: Choice preference attenuated when choice was decoupled from reliable information about eventual rewards; overall choice and informational contingency both mattered.
sources.supports: Own choice value can be partly instrumental, even where subjects also favor selecting among outcomes.
sources.does_not_support: Valuation by A of independent B's veto or B continuing identity, no subject-level motivation point-identification, no demonstrated AI intrinsic concern.

sources.title: Choosing (not) to choose: Uncovering intrinsic preferences for choice autonomy
sources.authors: Jana Freundt; Holger Herz; Leander Kopp
sources.reported_effect: Within a design controlling instrumental gains of choosing, a majority favors own choice while a meaningful minority prefers not choosing; results on OWN agency, not others'.
sources.data_availability: Data made available on request according to publisher
sources.supports: Own choice can have noninstrumental utility and heterogeneous signs.
sources.does_not_support: All agents want direct choice or A respects B when B voluntarily delegates.

sources.title: Paternalistic Interventions: Determinants of Demand and Supply
sources.supports: Original authors report that chooser consent-right regime raises chooser demand; distinct architect behavior must be separately evaluated.
sources.does_not_support: An increase in B's consent demand proves A's voluntary respect or a permanent intrinsic autonomy motive.
sources.ongoing_project: PR #361 contains additional checked author-table effects and nonsignificant architect-supply result; leave it DRAFT and don't relabel as independent outcome.

sources.title: When Decisions Require Consideration, People Give Up Control
sources.authors: Holly Dykstra; Christine Exley; Muriel Niederle; Heather Wong
sources.reported_effect: Requiring more consideration raises self-delegation preference, even among experienced subjects.
sources.supports: Voluntary delegation is sometimes a response to decision/consideration cost.
sources.does_not_support: A B who delegates is necessarily coerced or morally inferior; or autonomous AI prefers delegation.

sources.title: Delegation to artificial intelligence can increase dishonest behaviour
sources.reported_effect: Thirteen experiments; human principals sometimes induced cheating via delegated machine instructions; machine agents more likely than human agents to follow fully unethical instructions in compared tasks; mitigations incomplete.
sources.supports: Delegation and compliant AI outputs do not by themselves imply ethical voluntary cooperation.
sources.does_not_support: An agentic model autonomously values exploiting another original agent or lacks consciousness.

sources.title: Designing Human-AI Collaboration: A Sufficient-Statistic Approach
sources.reported_effect: In online fact-checking, people underreact to AI predictions and reduce effort when AI is confidently presented; optimal automation/assistance policy task-specific.
sources.supports: Human-AI assistance changes participant effort and beliefs; informational interventions are not passive.
sources.does_not_support: Optimal accuracy or performance policy ensures human self-determination, B consent or original B continuation.

sources.title: Trust, Delegation, and Alignment in Human-AI Decision Making
sources.reported_effect: Participant willingness to accept compensation to delegate AI decisions and actual prompt-choice alignment differ; significant reluctance despite moderate/high alignment.
sources.supports: Outcome alignment and freedom to delegate differ; human prompt encoding may be part of observed misalignment.
sources.does_not_support: AI independently values another agent's rights or B identity; no copyrighted full text mirrored.

critical_mismatch: Different empirical targets: OWN ability to decide vs OTHER B consent vs A provider voluntary response vs human-AI delegated action. These cannot be multiplied or averaged into one validated intrinsic original-B utility.
improvement_over_prior_cycles: Original publisher result plus inspected actual author R source, actual public file listings, script preflight blockers, bibliographic dedup and existing PR collision avoidance; zero invented test pass score.
priority_resolution: Independently inspect/execute Devine 2024 experiment 1 in a licensed R environment after reviewing 100 individual data-file privacy and original subject exclusions, exact R dependencies and full reproduction scripts.

Separate in independent datasets: B's informed consent demand, A's willingness to supply, and implemented outcomes. Existing PR #361 supply treatment may be nonsignificant; inspect its uncertainty and don't treat null as equivalence.
Where other-B protection is the estimand, measure A override/payoff and B authorized second-order choice; do not use OWN autonomy preference coefficient as outcome.
Any AI experiment must split principal instruction, AI compliance and original actor choice, and explicitly acknowledge ethics and non-equivalence to intrinsic independent AI preferences.
privacy_and_legal: Public author data must be reviewed for license, participant anonymity and permitted uses. Do not copy subject-level data or unlicensed manuscript into user's public repository.
release_gate: NOT_SCIENTIFIC_PROMOTION; publication version unchanged; external real original-B continuity and intrinsic will remain UNIDENTIFIED.
